title: Franklin D. Roosevelt and Churchill: The Atlantic Charter Conference — 1941
summary: In August 1941, off the coast of Newfoundland, President Franklin D. Roosevelt and Prime Minister Winston Churchill forged the historic Atlantic Charter aboard naval warships.
keywords: Historical Dialogue 150: ரூஸ்வெல்டும் சர்ச்சிலும்: ஸ்டாலினின் தந்திக்கு வந்த “முடியாத” பதில்
full_text:
In August 1941, amidst heavy fog off the coast of Placentia Bay, Newfoundland, two warships—the American heavy cruiser USS Augusta and the British battleship HMS Prince of Wales—anchored in deep secrecy.

United States President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill met face-to-face for the first time as wartime leaders. With Nazi forces sweeping across Europe and threatening civilization, their discussions transcended immediate tactical survival.

Roosevelt looked ahead to the post-war order, challenging Churchill on imperial sovereignty:
"Winston, this struggle cannot simply be about restoring the old status quo. When this nightmare is over, humanity must emerge into a world founded upon the Four Freedoms. Every nation, large or small, must possess the right of self-determination to choose its own form of government. The era of colonial empires is drawing to an inevitable close!"

Though Churchill was an ardent defender of the British Empire, he recognized the moral force of Roosevelt's vision and the absolute necessity of Anglo-American democratic solidarity.

Together, they signed the Atlantic Charter—an eight-point declaration affirming disarmament, sovereign equality, and global freedom that laid the cornerstone for the modern United Nations.
